items.title: Russia Senses Opportunity in Polish Political Turmoil
items.summary: After its sometime allies were ousted in elections in Hungary and Serbia, Moscow has seized on Poland’s constitutional standoff in its effort to weaken Europe’s support for Ukraine.

items.title: Why Orban and Vucic Broke With Trump on Election Denial
items.summary: Rejecting President Trump’s election denial playbook, nationalist leaders in Serbia and Hungary opted for an orderly retreat.

items.title: Trump Removes South Africa From the African Growth and Opportunity Act Trade Program
items.summary: The decision is the latest measure taken against the country, which the administration has accused of discriminating against white people.

items.title: Iran Says It Would Reopen Strait of Hormuz in 2 Days as Part of U.S. Deal
items.summary: Iranian officials spoke of some progress in negotiating to reopen the strait, a vital oil and gas shipping lane, even as they prepare for all-out war.

items.title: Netanyahu and Eisenkot Seek Shot to Be Israel’s Premier
items.summary: Party leaders will make competing cases to the Israeli president for either Benjamin Netanyahu or Gadi Eisenkot to get the first chance to build a governing coalition.

items.title: King Charles Meets Both Joy and Criticism on Caribbean Tour
items.summary: During the king’s visits to three former colonies, many people came out for celebratory parades and events. Others said the British state needed to atone for slavery’s toll.

items.title: Up in the Clouds With the Pope, It’s Still Commercial
items.summary: Unlike American presidents, Pope Leo XIV has no private jet, so he travels on commercial airlines, like the rest of us. Well, almost.

items.title: China’s Message to Its Rivals: You Need What We Make
items.summary: It’s not just rare earths. China is making it harder for other countries to shed their dependence on its solar, drone and drugmaking technology.

items.title: ‘This Hour Has 22 Minutes,’ a Canadian Sketch Show, Beats American Late Night to the Punchline
items.summary: The long-running comedy show “This Hour Has 22 Minutes” is having a heyday playing with the fraught relationship between President Trump and Canada.

items.title: India’s Congress Party Holds Mass Protest in New Delhi
items.summary: Tens of thousands gathered in India’s capital in a clamor of banging drums, chants and billowing flags, with participants from across the country.

items.title: Are Freezers Being Hacked? Europe and the U.S. Military Are Investigating.
items.summary: A wave of disruptions at grocery stores, which some officials blame on cyberattacks, highlight the vulnerability of supply chains. Shops across Europe were affected again on Monday.

items.title: He Pioneered a Groundbreaking Idea. And Was Met with Corporate Wrath.
items.summary: Economist William Nordhaus said putting a price on pollution was the best way to reduce climate change. Then came the fossil fuel lobby and the anti-tax movement.

items.title: Trump’s Tariffs Are On the Ballot in Michigan
items.summary: The levies as well as trade fighting with Canada are facing a test in the state, where voters appear skeptical of free trade but also of the president’s erratic approach.

items.title: Anthropic Reveals $17 Billion in Revenue as I.P.O. Approaches
items.summary: The A.I. company’s quarterly revenue totaled $17 billion, 12 times as high as the same quarter last year, while its net loss totaled $23 billion.

items.title: How A.I. Is Making It Easier Than Ever to Microtarget Voters
items.summary: Hyper-personalized messages, delivered with A.I.-enabled precision, herald a new frontier for voter outreach (and potential disinformation).

items.title: Martha Stewart Apologizes for Homeless Halloween Costume
items.summary: Stewart, the media mogul and entrepreneur, had posted a photo of a costume with tattered clothes and a sign asking for help.

items.title: Cracks in the A.I. Borrowing Binge
items.summary: Investors are growing increasingly concerned about the debt-fueled spending spree at the heart of the artificial intelligence buildout.

items.title: How The New York Times Is Covering the Midterm Elections
items.summary: More than 400 journalists across at least 30 states will interview voters, break down results and identify trends.

items.title: Disneyland’s Autopia Ride Will Switch to Electric Vehicles
items.summary: The gas-powered engines in Disneyland’s Autopia ride weren’t properly certified. The little cars will be replaced by E.V.s.

items.title: Gulf Economies, Torn by War in Iran, Desperately Need a Return to Normal
items.summary: States like Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates that have worked to rebalance from a dependence on energy have seen growth plunge in a year of strife.

items.title: Inside Anthropic’s Hunt for A.I. Computing Power
items.summary: The company went on a deal spree with tech giants, former crypto miners and others to gain computing power to further its artificial intelligence ambitions.

items.title: In San Francisco’s A.I. Boom, a First Date Has Become an Interview
items.summary: When there is A.I. to build, who has time for romance? Techies are going out less and expecting more on each date — including a family health history.

items.title: Driven by A.I. Boom, Marvell and Lumentum Announce $115 Billion Merger
items.summary: Marvell and Lumentum said they were combining, in a major bet on a technology, known as optical networking, that is increasingly being used in A.I. data centers.

items.title: Deportees Turn to TikTok to Document Life Starting Over
items.summary: On TikTok, men and women sent back after living in the United States are documenting the reality of starting over — and finding an audience.

items.title: Cyril Hilsum, Who Helped Invent Flat-Panel Displays in TVs and iPhones, Has Died at 101

items.title: How Binance’s $6.3 Billion Hack Went Down
items.summary: A war room. A global conference call. A founder who live-posted about the largest crypto heist in history. Inside a frantic 24 hours at the world’s biggest crypto exchange.

items.title: AO3 Fan Fiction Site Is Hacked and Could Be Offline for Weeks
items.summary: Home to tales inspired by the likes of “Harry Potter” and “Heated Rivalry,” the archive was taken down after “an intrusion,” one of its founders said. It could be down for weeks.
